core_obligations: Fit $Y' \to Y$ into a family of morphisms forming a $\tau$-covering: adjoin $\mathrm{id}_Y \to Y$ so the family is jointly surjective with every member flat, resp. flat and locally of finite presentation, resp. syntomic, resp. \'etale (proof line 1246-1249).

Apply $\tau$-locality on the target (definition-property-morphisms-local) to that covering: since $f$ has $\mathcal{P}$, each member of the covering base change has $\mathcal{P}$, in particular $Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$ (proof line 1246-1249).
proof_roadmap: Adjoin the identity to make the given morphism part of a $\tau$-covering.
Read off the base-changed property from $\tau$-locality on the target.
difficulty_reason: The single-sentence proof carries the whole argument: the given flat (resp. flat and lfp, syntomic, \'etale) morphism $Y' \to Y$ must be fitted, together with the identity, into a $\tau$-covering of $Y$ (jointly surjective, each member in the $\tau$ class), after which $\tau$-locality on the target applied to that covering gives the base-changed morphism has $\mathcal{P}$. The covering-family assembly is the one non-obvious step the sentence encodes.
